body.text:
1.a
oṃ namo ratnatrayāya
body.translated_text: Oṃ! Homage to the Three Jewels!

body.text:
2.b
  munivṛndavandyacaraṇo dhvastākhiladoṣa uttamaśrīkaḥ /
  sakalajagadarthadakṣo viśuddhabodhau jino jayati /
body.translated_text: He whose feet are revered by hosts of sages, whose faults are all destroyed, who is endowed with supreme glory, who is skilled in the welfare of the entire world — the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One) is triumphant in pure awakening!

children.translated_text: He who is glorious, whose lotus feet are unceasingly worshipped by gods and <s>asuras</s>,
who is directly the teacher of auspiciousness, a treasury of merit, a wish-fulfilling gem, the omniscient one,
who has completely uprooted the tangled net of faults, the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, who has reached the other shore —
may the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the lord of sages, the <s>Jina</s>, blazing with radiance, protect you!

body.text:
4.a
anantaram asyāvadānasya nidānam āha /
body.translated_text: Next, he narrated the introductory setting (<s>nidāna</s>) of this <s>avadāna</s> (narrative of noble deeds).

body.text: athāyuṣmān mahākāśyapo jānann eva parārthaṃ bhagavantam evam āha / bhagavan kadā kaṭhinam utpadyate / bhagavān āha / kārttikakṛṣṇapratipadam ārabhya triṃśad divaseṣu yad ahorātraṃ tatra saṃghasya kaṭhinam utpadyate /
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, knowing well [the answer] for the benefit of others, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, when does the <s>kaṭhina</s> (robe-offering ceremony) arise?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Beginning from the first day of the dark half of <s>Kārttika</s>, on whichever day-and-night within thirty days, there the <s>kaṭhina</s> arises for the <s>Saṃgha</s>.'

body.text:
6.a
tat sādhivāsam ānāpayitavyaṃ / kṛtakalpadaśārañjanā nīlasūtrasūcīśāstrakalpena tad dānapatayaḥ saṃnipatite saṃghe niḥsārāpayitavyāḥ / karmakārakeṇa bhikṣuṇā tato dānapatayo dānaparikarmakathayā pratisaṃmodayitavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: That should be accepted with consent. Having prepared dyeing according to the rules — with indigo thread, needle, and scissors according to proper procedure — the donors should be assembled before the gathered <s>Saṃgha</s>. The <s>bhikṣu</s> who is the officiator should then encourage the donors with an exhortation on the gift-giving procedure.

body.text:
6.b
tat sādhivāsetyādi / kaṭhinapradānaṃ kartukāmena dānapatinā 'ṣāḍhe śrāvaṇe vā māse savinayam upagamya kalpikakārakasya mukhenāryasaṃghasya vijñaptiḥ karaṇīyā tena caivaṃ karaṇīyā / samanvāharāryasaṃgha ayam amukanāmā kaṭhinam āstariṣyati / yadite 'ṅgīkaroty āryasaṃgho no cen nivārayatv iti / so pi tadā yadi dānapater āśayo viśuddhaḥ suviśuddhaṃ ca deyavastu syāt tadā tūṣṇībhāvena svīkuryān no cen nivārayet /
yadi tadādhivāsayaty āryasaṃghas tadā supramāṇāṃ surūpāṃ yugalīṃ rañjayitvā 'sya darśayet /
tataḥ kalpikakārakas tām ādāya dānapatiṃ visṛjya hastena māpayitvānayā kaṭhinacīvaraṃ kariṣyati / dānapatir iti tasmai pratipādayet / dvividhaṃ hi kaṭhinaṃ cīvaraṃ kṛtam akṛtakaṃ ca / tatra nikāyabhedena trikhaṇḍapañcakhaṇḍādikaṃ pariṇāhenānyūna trihastam āyāmenānyūna pañcahastaṃ susīvitaṃ kṛtakaṃ / akṛtadaśam asīvitam akṛtakaṃ / tat punaḥ pratyekaṃ dvividhaṃ niṣṭhitam aniṣṭḥitaṃ ca / tatra kṛtanīlabindukaṃ pūjāmantrādhivāsitan tan niṣṭhitakṛt / itarad aniṣṭhitaṃ / atrāśvinipūrṇamāsyaṃ dānapater [.. ..]ṇayā kālpikakārakaḥ / siddhaṃ kaṭhinacīvaram ādāyādhiṣṭhita traimāsasyāryasaṃghasya purastād evaṃ vadet / samanvāharāryyānena cīvareṇāsmiṃ saṃghāvāse 'mūkanāmā dānapatiḥ kaṭhinam āstariṣyati / adhivasatv āryasaṃghānumodayatu dānapatir iti / evaṃ dvir api trir api tad anv āryasaṃgho pi tad adhyeṣaṇām aṅgīkṛtya divā[.. .. ..]vā masīdravādinā nīlarāgarasena vā prānte catur bindūṃś catusatyādi viśuddhyā datvā trin vā triratnādi viśuddhyā dvau vā yogasaṃbhārādi viśuddhyā yathā vidhānam adhi(nu?)[..]yed etat /
body.translated_text: Regarding 'that should be accepted with consent' and so forth: a donor wishing to make the <s>kaṭhina</s> offering, in the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s> or <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, having respectfully approached, should make a formal announcement to the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> through the mouth of the officiator, and should do so thus: 'May the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> take note — this [donor] named so-and-so will spread the <s>kaṭhina</s>. If the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> accepts it, [well]; if not, let it refuse.' At that time, if the donor's intention is pure and the material to be given is well-purified, the <s>Saṃgha</s> should accept by silence; if not, it should refuse. If the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> then accepts, having dyed a pair [of cloth pieces] of proper measure and good quality, it should be shown to him. Then the officiator, taking it, dismissing the donor, having measured it by hand — 'with this the <s>kaṭhina</s> robe will be made' — should hand it over to the donor, saying 'donor.' For the <s>kaṭhina</s> robe is of two kinds: finished and unfinished. Among these, according to the division of schools, a robe of three panels, five panels, and so forth, not less than three <s>hastas</s> (cubits) in breadth and not less than five <s>hastas</s> in length, well-sewn, is 'finished.' One with unfinished edges, unsewn, is 'unfinished.' Each of these again is of two kinds: completed and uncompleted. Among these, one that has the blue dot applied and has been consecrated with offering mantras is 'completed.' The other is 'uncompleted.' Here, on the full moon of <s>Āśvinī</s>, the officiator [...] for the donor. Having taken the completed <s>kaṭhina</s> robe, before the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> that has observed the three-month [rain retreat], he should say thus: 'May the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> take note — with this robe, in this monastery, the donor named so-and-so will spread the <s>kaṭhina</s>. May the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> consent and approve, [saying] "donor."' Thus a second and third time. And the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> too, having accepted that petition, by day [...] or with ink-fluid, or with indigo dye, having placed four dots at the border for the purification of the four truths and so forth, or three for the purification of the three jewels and so forth, or two for the purification of the two accumulations and so forth, should consecrate it according to the prescribed procedure.

body.text: prabhātāyān tu nisāyāṃ parikalpitesūpasṛṣṭe samucchritātapatradhvajapatākā digvidig vinyastakhaṇḍapiṇḍadhūpaghaṭikojjvalayaṣṭipradīpasugandhagandhādidivyasurabhikusumāvakīrṇe pradeśe khaṭvāyām mañcāyām vā pṛthupīṭhake mantrādhiṣṭhitaṃ pañcabhir upahārair abhyarcitaṃ kaṭhinacīvaraṃ prasārya pratiṣṭhāpayet / tad anu tac chrāddho dānapatir udārābhiḥ pūjābhir abhipūjyābhipraṇamya suvarṇarajatatāmrādidhātu dravyaṃ marakatapadmarāgavajravaidūryyendranīlādikaṃ ratnaṃ divyāmbarābharaṇādikaṃ ca tasmin kaṭhinacīvare ratnatrayāya dadyāt // kṣetraṃ vādikā gṛhārāmopavanādikaṃ dāsīdāsahastyaś ca gomahiṣyādikaṃ piṇḍakādipratyāyaṃ ca bahirdhanantāḍapatrādau tan nāmākam vilikhya tatraiva prayacchet / bhakṣyabhojyalehyapeyādikaṃ bhājanādīni pañcopakaraṇabhāṇḍāni śayanāsanādīni bhaiṣajyāny upakaraṇāni cānekāny upabhogārhāṇi vastūni kaṭhinaṃ saṃspṛśya tat pārśvataḥ saṃghopabhogāya viśrāṇayet / iti kaṭhinaṃ /
body.translated_text: When the night has dawned, in a place that has been prepared — with raised parasols, banners, and flags erected, with incense-pots, vessels, brilliant lamps, fragrant scents, and divine sweet-smelling flowers scattered in every direction and intermediate direction, on a clean ground — on a couch, bed, or broad seat, the <s>kaṭhina</s> robe, consecrated with <s>mantras</s>, honored with the five offerings, should be spread out and established. Then that faithful donor, having worshipped with magnificent offerings and bowed in homage, should give to the Three Jewels upon that <s>kaṭhina</s> robe: substances of gold, silver, copper, and other metals; gems such as emeralds, rubies, diamonds, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, sapphires, and the like; divine garments, ornaments, and such. Fields, platforms, houses, gardens, groves, and the like; male and female servants, elephants, cows, buffaloes, and the like; food and other requisites — having inscribed their name on external wealth such as parasols and the like, he should offer them right there. Eatables, drinkables, lickables, sippables, and the like; vessels and such; the five kinds of equipment; beds and seats; medicines; implements and many items worthy of use — having touched the <s>kaṭhina</s>, he should distribute them beside it for the enjoyment of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. Thus is the <s>kaṭhina</s>.

body.text:
7.b
athāyuṣmān sumanā nāma bhikṣur bhagavantam etad avocat // bhagavan kena kāraṇena cīvarādikaṃ kaṭhinam ity ucyate / bhagavān āha / āyuṣman dṛḍhaṃ viśuddham abhedyaṃ vipulāvināśi ca kaṭhinam ity ucyate / tathā hi dānapater āśayasya dṛḍhatvāc cīvarasya viśuddhatvāt saṃghasyābhedyatvād dānasya phalasya ca vipulāvināśitvāc ca sarvam eva kaṭhinaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>bhikṣu</s> named <s>Sumanā</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, for what reason are robes and such called <s>kaṭhina</s> (lit. "hard, firm")?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Venerable one, it is called <s>kaṭhina</s> because it is firm, pure, indestructible, and vast and imperishable. For because the donor's intention is firm, because the robe is pure, because the <s>Saṃgha</s> is indestructible, and because the fruit of the gift is vast and imperishable — all of this is indeed <s>kaṭhina</s>.'

children.translated_text: In the city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the charioteer who tames men,
having dwelt there, his mind freed from all bonds,
with faculties at peace and mind tranquil,
the <s>Jina</s> invited his disciples.

children.text: śrāvastyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme śubhe surabhidhūpadhūpite sugandhipuṣpaprakaropaśobhite śuciparisare mahārham mahadāsana-m-āsīnaṃ viśuddhabodhiṃ vidhvastasamastadḥsaṃ mahākāruṇikaṃ bhagavantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ śākyamunīndraṃ mahatpariṣadgaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ viharati sma / atha bhagavān tūṣṇībhāvenāvasthitaḥ san sattvārthaṃ prati daśavidhabuddhakṛtyakaraṇāya laukikaṃ cittam etc., v.  22
children.translated_text: In the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the garden of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> — lovely, perfumed with fragrant incense, adorned with clusters of sweet-smelling flowers, with clean surroundings — seated on a great and valuable seat, the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, lord of the <s>Śākyas</s>, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, of pure awakening, with all faults destroyed, the greatly compassionate one, was dwelling together with the great assembly of attendants. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, remaining in silence, with a worldly thought for the sake of beings, in order to perform the ten kinds of <s>Buddha</s>-activities, etc., [see] verse 22.

body.text:
9.
tataḥ tīrthikaparivrājakacoditāyās tathāgataṃ prati duṣkṛtaṃ karma saṃsmṛtya saṃjātasaṃvegāḥ sthavirasthāvirā bhikṣavaḥ śirasi vinihitāñjalayo mahadāsanāsīnaṃ mahākāruṇikaṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ praṇipatyedam abrūvan /
body.translated_text: Then the elder monks, the senior <s>bhikṣus</s>, having recalled the wrongdoing committed toward the <s>Tathāgata</s> instigated by <s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, were seized with remorse. With palms joined above their heads, they bowed to the greatly compassionate <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> seated on the great seat and spoke thus:

body.text:
10.
kṛtā bhagavatānekā dharmādhikārikī kathā vyākṛtāś cāneke sattvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau /
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has given many discourses on the <s>Dharma</s> and its subject matter, and has given prophecies to many beings regarding unsurpassed, perfect awakening.'

body.text:
11.a
tad anv anavatapte bhagavatḥ purastāt svakasvakāṃ karmaplotiṃ vyākurmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Following that, at <s>Anavatapta</s>, before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, let us declare each our own <s>karmaploti</s> (narrative of past deeds).'

body.text:
12.b
dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jīvatāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ dhriyamāṇānāṃ yāpayatām daśāvaśyakaraṇīyāni bhavanti // katamāni daśa / na tāvad buddhā bhagavantaḥ parinirvānti / yāvan na buddhaṃ vyākurvanti / yāvad anekena sattvenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ notpāditaṃ bhavati / yāvan na sarve vineyā vinītā bhavanti / yāvac chrāvakayugam agratāyāṃ na nirdiṣṭaṃ bhavati / yāvan na sīmābandhaḥ kṛto bhavati / yāvan nāyuṣaḥ pañcamo bhāga utsṛṣṭo bhavati / yāvan na śrāvastyām mahānagaryāṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ darśitaṃ bhavati / yāvan na śāṃkāśye nagare devāvatāram darśitaṃ bhavati / yāvan na mātāpitarau satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitau bhavataḥ / yāvad anavatapte mahāsarasi pūrvikā karmaplotiḥ śrāvakasaṅghena sārdhaṃ na vyākṛtā bhavatīti /
body.translated_text: For it is the nature of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, while living, abiding, remaining, and carrying on, that there are ten things that must necessarily be done. What are the ten? <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> do not pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> until they have given a prophecy of Buddhahood; until many beings have generated the mind of unsurpassed, perfect awakening; until all those to be trained have been trained; until a pair of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) has been designated as foremost; until the boundary demarcation has been made; until a fifth of their lifespan has been relinquished; until the great miracle has been displayed in the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>; until the descent from the gods has been displayed in the city of <s>Sāṃkāśya</s>; until their mother and father have been established in the truths; and until the narrative of past deeds has been declared together with the <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Saṃgha</s> at the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>.

body.text:
13.a
atha bhagavatā manasi kṛtvā śrāvakasaṃghena sārdhaṃ vyākṛtā bhavatīti / bhagavan pūrvikāṃ karmaplotim anavatapte vyākartukāmo bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having considered, 'It shall be declared together with the <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Saṃgha</s>,' desiring to declare the narrative of past deeds at <s>Anavatapta</s>, addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s> thus:

children.translated_text: Having heard that utterance of the great sage,
having received the command of the <s>Sugata</s>, the disciples,
those foremost beings, then flew through the sky by supernatural power,
like geese following the king of geese.

body.text: yathaivānyahaṃsagaṇaparivṛtas tathaiva buddho bhagavān śākyamuniḥ /
body.translated_text: Just as [a king of geese] is surrounded by other flocks of geese, even so the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>,

body.text:
15
visphuradvicitramarīcijāla ekonaiḥ pañcabhir arhacchataiḥ sārdhaṃ lohitapakṣaiḥ pakṣibhiḥ parivṛto guratmān iva vihāyasā jetavanād vihārān
niragāt /
body.translated_text: with a blazing net of brilliant, variegated rays, together with four hundred and ninety-nine <s>Arhats</s>, like <s>Garuḍa</s> (the king of birds) surrounded by red-winged birds, departed through the sky from the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery.

body.text:
16
ekonapañcaśatavītarāgeṇa sārdhaṃ gatavān /
body.translated_text: Together with the four hundred and ninety-nine passion-free ones, he went.

body.text:
17
atha bhagavān mahāśrāvakasaṃghena saha śrāvastyām antarhitaḥ himavaduttarasthagandhamādanaparvatasyottareṇa mahākīṭaparvatasyāgre
'navatapte mahāsarasi pratyasthāt /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, together with the great assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s>, having vanished from <s>Śrāvastī</s>, arrived at the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>, on the summit of the great <s>Kīṭa</s> mountain, to the north of Mount <s>Gandhamādana</s>, north of the <s>Himalayas</s>.

body.text:
18
na vidyate rāgādikleśasaṃtāpo yasmin sarasi / tad anavataptaṃ mahāsaraḥ / tac ca / ekaikapārśvena catuścatvāriṃśad yojanāni / adhaś catvāriṃśad yojanāni /
body.translated_text: There exists no burning heat of passion and other afflictions in that lake; hence it is [called] <s>Anavatapta</s> ("Without Heat"), the great lake. And it is forty-four <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) on each side and forty <s>yojanas</s> deep.

children.translated_text: That delightful [lake], frequented by <s>vyāḍas</s> (fierce beings) and <s>yakṣas</s>,
beautifully adorned with trees bearing variegated flowers,
from which four rivers, flowing toward the ocean,
stream forth in the four directions.

children.text: gaṅgā ca sindhuś ca nadaś ca vakṣuḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and the <s>Sindhu</s>, and the river <s>Vakṣu</s>,

children.text: śītā ca yān naiva taranti martyāḥ /
children.translated_text: and the <s>Śītā</s> — which no mortals can cross,
except one who has obtained the power of supernatural ability (<s>ṛddhi</s>) —
come, let me go to this lake, [vast as] the great ocean!

body.text:
21.1.a
vicitrapuṣpair nānāprakāraiḥ svādusugandhiphalavṛkṣaiḥ suśobhitam /
body.translated_text: Beautifully adorned with variegated flowers of many kinds and with trees bearing sweet, fragrant fruits.

body.text:
21.2
punaḥ śītalāmalasvādusalilasampūrṇam /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, filled with cool, pure, sweet water.

body.text:
21.3
kamalakuvalayakumudakahlārakokanadādiprasūnopaśobhitam /
body.translated_text: Adorned with blossoms of <s>kamala</s> (lotus), <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotus), <s>kumuda</s> (white water-lily), <s>kahlāra</s> (white lotus), <s>kokanada</s> (red lotus), and the like.

body.text:
21.4
punaḥ sārasaśarāricakrāṅgabakabalākākurarakrauñcādivividhavihaṃgarāvaramaṇīyam /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, delightful with the cries of various birds such as <s>sārasa</s> (cranes), <s>śarāri</s> (ospreys), <s>cakrāṅga</s> (ruddy sheldrakes), <s>baka</s> (herons), <s>balākā</s> (white cranes), <s>kurara</s> (fish-eagles), <s>krauñca</s> (curlews), and others.

body.text:
21.5
punar makarandapānalampaṭabhramarāṃganāgaṇagītopakūjitam /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, resonant with the humming songs of swarms of female bees intoxicated by drinking nectar.

body.text:
21.6.b
surāsuramunikinnarayakṣarākṣasoragāpsarāgaṇopaśobhitam /
body.translated_text: Adorned by hosts of gods, <s>asuras</s>, sages, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>uragas</s> (serpents), and <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs).

body.text:
22
atha tatra buddho bhagavāṃl laukikaṃ cittam utpādayati /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> generated a worldly thought there.

body.text: tadāntaśaḥ kuntapipīlikādayo bhagavataś cetasā cittam ājānate / atha nandopanandau nāgarājāv evaṃ saṃlakṣayataḥ kiṃkāraṇaṃ bhagavatedaṃ cittam utpāditam anavatapte mahāsarasi karmaplotikāṃ vyākartukāma iti buddhādhiṣṭhānena jñātvā tābhyām anavatapte mahāsarasi madhye śakaṭacakrapramāṇaṃ sahasradalaṃ vilasanmaṇinālakaṃ suhīrakesaram pañcaratnamayaṃ bhagavata āsanārthaṃ sauvarṇasaroruhaṃ vinirmitaṃ tatra bhagavān niṣasāda bhikṣavo 'pi bhagavato 'bhisaṃmukham anyāsu kamalakarṇikāsu niṣaṇṇāḥ
body.translated_text: At that moment, even the ants and insects understood the <s>Bhagavān's</s> thought with their minds. Then the <s>nāga</s> kings <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s> reflected thus: 'For what reason has the <s>Bhagavān</s> generated this thought?' Knowing through the <s>Buddha's</s> supernatural empowerment that he wished to declare the narrative of past deeds at the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>, the two of them fashioned in the middle of the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s> a golden lotus — the size of a cart-wheel, with a thousand petals, with a stalk of sparkling jewels, with fine pistils, made of the five precious substances — as a seat for the <s>Bhagavān</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> sat down. The <s>bhikṣus</s> too sat down on other lotus seats facing the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.translated_text: Now at that time, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> was standing on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, sewing his outer robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>). There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Go, <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, bring [our] companion in renunciation.' 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>,' the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words, vanished from the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s> and appeared on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain. Before the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, he spoke thus: 'O <s>Śāriputra</s>! The Teacher, together with four hundred and ninety-nine <s>Arhats</s>, wishes to declare the narrative of past deeds at the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s> and stands waiting for you. Come, let us go.' <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, let me first sew my outer robe; I will come afterward.' Then <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, unable to tolerate those words, bound his five fingers by supernatural power. But <s>Śāriputra</s>, by his own great power, remained standing, sewing as before. 'Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, if that is so, let the robe-thread be [released]!' <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> said: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, if you will not go, the robe must first be finished sewing; after that you shall go. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, I shall render assistance.' <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Do so.' Then the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> began to sew with his five fingers by his supernatural power. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to him: 'Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, if that is so, let it be a different thread.' He said: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, having done this, if you still will not go, I shall take you by the power of <s>ṛddhi</s>.' Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, extending his waist-band, said: 'You, Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, have been designated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as foremost among those possessing supernatural power. But this much first — you would take me by force?' Then the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> pulled him. Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> reflected: 'He is of great supernatural power and great might. It is possible that he will pull [me] away when I am bound.' Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> anchored himself to <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain. The Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> pulled — along with <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> reflected: 'He will drag even <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain.' Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> anchored himself to <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains. The Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> pulled. Then even <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, was shaken. Then the <s>nāga</s> kings <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s> were also disturbed. When they were disturbed, the <s>bhikṣus</s> asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Why, <s>Bhagavān</s>, are the <s>nāga</s> kings <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s> disturbed, causing the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s> to tremble?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Bhikṣus</s>, the <s>nāga</s> kings <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s> are not disturbed. Rather, the two great <s>śrāvakas</s> are performing a great display of supernatural power against each other.' Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> reflected: 'He will drag even <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains.' So he anchored himself to the lotus stalk of the very lotus seat upon which the <s>Bhagavān</s> was seated. Then he stood immovable. The Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> said to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'You have performed a great display of supernatural power. Very well — come, let us go.' Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, I too shall come alone; please, let the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> go first.' Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, going first, having bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet, sat down on his own lotus seat. Afterward the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> arrived and took his own seat. He said to him: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, you have arrived!' He replied: 'I have arrived.'

body.translated_text: Then all the <s>bhikṣus</s>, having become doubtful, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Look, Venerable Sir! The <s>Bhagavān</s> has designated the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> — of great supernatural power and great might — as foremost among those possessing supernatural power. Yet even he was defeated in supernatural power by the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Bhikṣus</s>, not only now — even in the past, he was defeated by this one through skill.'

body.translated_text:
25
Now listen to this. In the past, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, there was a master painter in <s>Madhyadeśa</s> (the Central Country). Having some business, he went to the <s>Yavana</s> territory (Greek lands) and lodged at the house of a master automaton-maker, where he took food and other things and settled in. The automaton-maker made a wooden automaton puppet and sent it as an attendant-maidservant. This wooden automaton puppet stood holding massage oil in her hand. Then he said to her, 'Come here.' She stood silently. He thought, 'Surely an attendant-maidservant has been sent for my service.' He praised her: 'Ah, what a jewel among women has been fashioned by the Creator! By her the merit of my eyes has been purified.' 'Shame on the birth in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> of that man for whom such a young woman, endowed with beauty and youth, supremely lovely, would not be touched by eye, hand, or bodily contact!' Having been thus flattered by these nectar-like sweet words, he began to embrace her: 'Come, come, O beautiful dear one!' Even so the wooden automaton puppet said nothing. Having determined this, with his mind consumed by desire, he quickly approached; he seized her by the hand and pulled, and thereupon a heap of wooden joint-pieces was left standing. He was humiliated and mocked. He thought: 'I alone have been humiliated by this man. I too shall do likewise, so that he will be mocked and humiliated in the midst of the royal assembly.' Thinking thus, he painted on the wall facing the door a self-hanging figure with a noose around the neck. Then he hid behind the door panel and remained. When the automaton-maker's return time had passed, the automaton-maker thought: 'It is too late. For whose sake does he not come out?' He went there and saw it. Having seen it, he thought: 'Why has he hung himself?' Then he noticed the pile of wooden joint-pieces and realized: 'Having been humiliated, he has hung himself.' Now it was the custom in the <s>Yavana</s> territory that if a guest dies in someone's house, the host must perform the funeral rites only after reporting to the king. He reported to the king: 'Your Majesty, a master painter from <s>Madhyadeśa</s> came here and lodged at my house. I sent a wooden automaton puppet as a maidservant. He seized her by the hand and pulled, and thereupon a heap of wooden joint-pieces remained. Having been humiliated, he hung himself. Let Your Majesty inspect this, and then I shall perform the funeral rites.' By the king's order, ministers went there. They saw it. Having seen it, they said: 'How shall we take him down from the hook?' Others said: 'The noose must be cut.' He took an axe and began to cut the noose. When it was cut, the automaton-maker was humiliated and stood exposed. The painter emerged from behind the door panel and said: 'You, sir, humiliated me when I was alone. But you have been humiliated by me in the midst of the royal assembly.' What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>? He who was the master painter — he is none other than the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Śāriputra</s>. He who was the master automaton-maker — he is none other than the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>. Even then he was defeated by this very skill; now too he has been defeated by this one.

body.translated_text:
26
Hear further how he was defeated by this one. In the past, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, a dispute arose between two master painters. One said: 'I know excellent craftsmanship.' The other said: 'I know excellent craftsmanship.' Then, from the dispute, they both went before the king. Before the king they declared: 'I know excellent craftsmanship.' The other too said: 'I know excellent craftsmanship.' Then the king showed them a gate-chamber: 'Gentlemen, I do not know which of you knows the craft. But let each of you work on one wall.' And the second on the other wall. Then, giving them a curtain between, they began to work. One completed his painting in six months. The second also completed his wall-preparation in six months. The one who had done the painting went before the king. Having approached, he said: 'Your Majesty, my painting is complete. Great King, please inspect it.' The king went out with his ministers. The king saw it and said: 'This painting is excellent.' The second also said: 'Your Majesty, please inspect the painted work.' The reflection fell upon it. The king, having seen that, said: 'This painted work is clearer.' He then pulled aside the curtain and said: 'This is not painting, but wall-preparation.' Thus the king was amazed. He addressed the ministers: 'Sirs, this one's craftsmanship is superior.' What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>? He who completed the wall-preparation in six months — he is none other than the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Śāriputra</s>. He who completed the painting in six months — he is none other than the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>. Even then he was defeated in craftsmanship; now too he has been defeated by him in supernatural power.

<s>Likhita</s>, out of compassion, fashioned a clay head for him;
then at sunrise it suddenly shattered into a hundred pieces upon the earth.
In another birth, that <s>Śaṅkha</s> has now become <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>;

children.text: likhitaḥ śāriputro 'yaṃ tad vijetā tadāpy abhūt //
children.translated_text: this <s>Likhita</s> is <s>Śāriputra</s> — even then he was the victor.

body.text: etarhy apy anena rddhyā parājita ityādi vistarato jñeyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Now too he has been defeated by this one in supernatural power, and so forth — this should be understood in detail.

body.text:
28.b
yāsāṃ dhyānasamāpattīnāṃ lābhī tathāgatas tāsāṃ pratyekabuddhā nāmāpi na jānate / yāsāṃ pratyekabuddhā lābhinas tāsāṃ śāriputro nāmāpi na jānīte / yāsāṃ lābhī śāriputras tāsāṃ maudgalyāyano nāmāpi na jānīte / yāsāṃ lābhī maudgalyāyanas tāsāṃ tadanye śrāvakā nāmāpi na jānate / ato 'yaṃ maharddhiko mahānubhāvo 'yaṃ śāriputro maudgalyāyanāt kiṃtu bahulavihāriṇāṃ saṃdhāya maya rddhimatām agrata iti nirdiṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: 28.b. Of whatever <s>dhyāna</s>-attainments and <s>samāpattis</s> the <s>Tathāgata</s> is a gainer, the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> do not even know the names. Of whatever the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> are gainers, <s>Śāriputra</s> does not even know the names. Of whatever <s>Śāriputra</s> is a gainer, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> does not even know the names. Of whatever <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> is a gainer, the other <s>śrāvakas</s> do not even know the names. Therefore this <s>Śāriputra</s> is of great supernatural power and great might, [superior to] <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>; but with reference to those who most frequently abide [in supernatural power], <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> has been designated by me as foremost among those possessing supernatural power.

body.text:
29
29.1.a
ity anantaram āha /

children.translated_text: Having gone there, let him utter a speech
in accordance with the conduct of former lives.
He who remembers here shall there declare
the wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s> and its resultant happiness.

body.translated_text: 29 / 29.1.a / After that, he said:

body.text:
29.2.a
atha sthavirasthavirā bhikṣavas tathāgatājñayā svakasvakaṃ karmaplotikaṃ vyākurvanti / prathamataram mahāpratibhāno nāgila āha /

children.text: nāgilo nāma nāmena bhikṣur buddhasya śrāvakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣu</s> named <s>Nāgila</s>, a disciple of the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: praśnaṃ pṛṣṭo vyākārṣīd anavatapte mahāhrade sarasi //
children.translated_text: when questioned, declared his answer at the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>.

body.translated_text: 29.2.a. Then the elder monks, the senior <s>bhikṣus</s>, by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s command, each declared their own <s>karmaploti</s> (narrative of past deeds). First, <s>Nāgila</s>, of great eloquence, spoke:

body.text: tato nāgilo nāma bhikṣus tathāgatasyāgrato daśanakhāñjaliṃ kṛtvā svakāṃ karmaplotikāṃ vyārocayati sma /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣu</s> named <s>Nāgila</s>, having made an <s>añjali</s> (salutation) with his ten fingertips before the <s>Tathāgata</s>, declared his own <s>karmaploti</s> (narrative of past deeds):

children.translated_text: Having given the <s>kaṭhina</s> to the <s>Saṃgha</s> with a well-pleased mind,
for thirty great <s>kalpas</s> henceforth I do not know of a bad rebirth. || 1
For eighteen <s>kalpas</s> I have delighted in the heavenly world;

children.text: catuḥṣaṣṭiṃ tu vārāṇi devendratvaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā // 2
children.translated_text: sixty-four times I have been <s>Devendra</s> (Lord of the gods). || 2
Eight thousand times I have become a <s>Cakravartin</s> (Universal Monarch);

children.text: prādeśikānāṃ rājñāṃ tu saṃkhyā mama na vidyate // 3
children.translated_text: of regional kings, my number is beyond count. || 3

children.text: aho ratnatraye kārāṃ kurvanti yatra mānavāḥ /
children.translated_text: Ah, when men perform service to the Three Jewels,

children.text: parīttamātraṃ dattvā tu labhante vipulaṃ phalam // 4
children.translated_text: having given but a small offering, they obtain abundant fruit! || 4

children.text: yadi martyeṣu me janma hitvā divyaṃ sukhaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: If my birth be among mortals, having abandoned the great happiness of the gods,
I am worshipped among mortals — that is the fruit of <s>kaṭhina</s> donation. (5)

children.text: yadi devopapattiḥ syāt tyaktvā mānuṣyakaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: If there be a divine rebirth, having abandoned human happiness,

children.text: devasaṃghasya pūjyo ' smi kaṭhinadānasya tat phalam // 6
children.translated_text: I am worshipped by the assembly of gods — that is the fruit of <s>kaṭhina</s> donation. (6)
Taking the <s>Cakravāḍa</s> (world-encircling mountain range), the disk of the earth and ocean,
if I wish, I can cover it all right now with fine garments! (7)
Furthermore, proclaiming the excellence of <s>kaṭhina</s> donation, he said:
At every step I take, fine garments appear before me;

children.text: dūṣyopari ca tiṣṭhāmi dūṣyaṃ cāpi vitānakam // 8
children.translated_text: I stand upon fine garments, and fine garments form a canopy above. (8)

children.text: bhavā udghāṭitā mahyaṃ kleśāś cādhyāsitā mayā /
children.translated_text: The doors of existence have been opened for me, and the afflictions have been overcome by me;
all outflows (<s>āsravas</s>) have been exhausted — that is the fruit of <s>kaṭhina</s> donation. (9)
The four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvids</s>) and likewise the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣas</s>),

children.text: ṣaḍ abhijñā hy anuprāptāḥ kṛtaṃ buddhasya śāsanam // 10
children.translated_text: the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñās</s>) have been attained — the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> has been fulfilled. (10)
One of fragrant body, going to the world of gods,
of great wealth, possessing enjoyments, a seeker of happiness,
the fragrance of whose pure moral conduct wafts in all directions —
through the gift of fragrance, indeed, one becomes a traveler to liberation. [Fragrance]

children.text: puṣpaṃ ye sugatasya saṃghasamitau dāsyanti śraddhānvitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who, endowed with faith, give flowers at the assembly of the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the <s>Sugata</s> —
they shine like flowers, going to heaven, attaining liberation, for the benefit of all the world;
they are worshipped unceasingly by gods and <s>asuras</s>, endowed with the fragrance of good conduct;

children.text: kāyād gandhavaraṃ prayāti sukhino ghrāṇendriyaṃ śudhyati //
children.translated_text: from their bodies excellent fragrance issues forth; the happy ones — their sense of smell is purified.
One should offer a variegated thick garland in the assembly of gods;
one will not suffer from headaches and will become a sky-goer. [Flowers]

children.text: ye dhūpaṃ pradadanti manmatharipoḥ saṃghāya sadbhāvatas
children.translated_text: Those who give incense to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the enemy of desire (<s>Manmatha</s>), with sincere devotion —

children.text: te nityaṃ sukham āpnuvanti sukhitā bhogeśvarāḥ śīlinaḥ /
children.translated_text: they always obtain happiness, are happy, lords of enjoyments, virtuous;

children.text: na bhrāntasmṛtayo bhavanti vaśino dhyāneṣu labdhāspadāḥ
children.translated_text: they do not become confused in memory, are self-controlled, established in the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations);

children.text: śāntiṃ yānti manoharāḥ paṭudhiyaḥ pūjyāḥ sadevāsuraiḥ // dhūpa
children.translated_text: they attain peace, are captivating, of sharp intelligence, worthy of worship by gods and <s>asuras</s>. [Incense]
Delightful to the eye, with a well-filled treasury,
one becomes possessed of large, blue eyes,
worthy of being gazed upon by women and men —
one who offers a garland of lamps in the <s>Saṃgha</s>. [Lamps]
Of clear complexion, with soft hands and feet,
of great strength, unconquerable by enemies —
through the gift of oil, mortals become
possessed of beautiful forms and attain happiness. [Oil]
One who gives footwear with a joyful mind
will gain supernatural power, become rich in wealth,
will have a well-formed pair of feet, be great-souled,
a traveler to heaven, a rider of excellent vehicles.
When the Sage, born first on earth,
strode forth with powerful steps — seven in number —
a row of lotuses was produced; and that fruit —

children.text: sā pādukāyugaladānam ṛte kutaḥ syāt // upānaha
children.translated_text: how could it be without the gift of a pair of sandals? [Footwear]
One becomes a sheltering canopy for the world through the gift of a parasol;
one dwells long in the pleasant shade, in the delight of royal splendor;
one certainly becomes a lord of the <s>Dharma</s>, a protector of the entire world —
such a one does not go to the dense thicket of lower births; handsome and a gainer of enjoyments.
The great-souled one, having joyfully first raised
a parasol over the relic-shrine of <s>Kāśyapa</s>,
having enjoyed happiness in heaven and on earth,
<s>Nanda</s>, the great-souled one, attained tranquility. [Parasol]
One certainly gains wisdom through the gift of thread and needle;
through gaining wisdom, one is freed from the fears of the rounds of existence — a treasury of intelligence;

children.text: prajñā rājñī duritaharaṇe nāsti kācit tayānyā
children.translated_text: wisdom is the queen in the removal of evil deeds; there is none other like her —

children.text: sā saṃpannā bhavati saphala saṃpadā sarvathaiva // sūtrasūcī
children.translated_text: when she is attained, she becomes fruitful, yielding prosperity in every way. [Thread and Needle]
One who here gives chalk (<s>khaṭikā</s>), pure as crystal,

children.text: khaṭikāṃ yo dadātiha jāyate paṇḍito mahān // khaṭikā
children.translated_text: even twelve finger-breadths [in size], is born as a great scholar. [Chalk]
Endowed with enjoyments, with a face that captivates the eyes and is fragrant, with a pleasant voice free from phlegm and disease,
free from mental afflictions, partaking of divine birth —
these are the results that beautifully sprout from the gift of betel (<s>tāmbūla</s>). (1)

body.text:
30.10.2
  śrīlakṣaṇāṅkitamukho nayanābhirāmas
  tāmrādharaḥ sarucikomaladantapaṅktiḥ / śleṣmāmayakrimivivarjitacārugaṇḍas
  tāmbūladānavihitaṃ phalam etad agram // 2 // tāmbūla
body.translated_text: With a face marked by the signs of <s>Śrī</s> (beauty), delightful to the eyes, with red lips, with a radiant and soft row of teeth, with beautiful cheeks free from phlegm disease and worms — this is the supreme fruit of the gift of betel. (2) [Betel]

children.translated_text: For the body adorned with [ornaments] on the neck, head, feet, and arms,
made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> and gold, set with pearls,

children.text: gātrasya bhūṣaṇavidher divi vā kṣitau vā
children.translated_text: whether in heaven or on earth, the best adornment of the body
as prescribed — the learned declare to be cloth. (1)
Though one be possessed of beauty, of good family, discerning,
though one has labored in many scriptural systems,
though one be adorned with hosts of virtues such as moral conduct —

children.text: na bhrājate hi bhuvi vastram ṛte manuṣyaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: a person does not shine on earth without cloth. (2)

children.text: tasmād vibhūṣaṇam atulyam avekṣyavastraṃ śītoṣṇadaṃśamaśakaprativāraṇaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, seeing that cloth is an incomparable adornment and a protection against cold, heat, gadflies, and mosquitoes,
the garment of modesty being peerless —
the gift of cloth should be given again and again by people who desire their goals. (3)
With fly-whisks glittering like moonbeams, with golden handles,
seated upon a lion-throne, with white parasols,
adorned on the head with crowns of gold and jewels —

children.text: śrīcakravartir api vastram ṛte na bhāti // 4
children.translated_text: even the glorious <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) does not shine without cloth. (4)
The glorious lord of wealth (<s>Dhanendra</s>) dwelling in the city of <s>Alakā</s>, in <s>Bhogavatī</s> adorned with a thousand gem-tongued [serpents],
on the peaks of <s>Kailāsa</s> and <s>Meru</s>, amidst the assembly of gods —
even <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Rudra</s> do not shine without cloth. (5)
Having given a beautiful garland of cluster-woven robes — tawny, variegated,

children.text: raktaiś cānyaiś ca ramyaiḥ suruciravasanaiś cīvaraiś cārumālām /
children.translated_text: blue, yellow, white, red, and other lovely, very fine garments — as <s>cīvaras</s> (monastic robes),
or divine cloth or released garments, to the assembly of the <s>Sugata's</s> sons — one becomes well-formed, delightful,

children.text: hrīvastrālaṅkṛtātmā bhavati paṭumatiḥ sarvadharmeśvaraḥ saḥ // vastra
children.translated_text: adorned with the garment of modesty, of sharp intelligence, a lord of all <s>dharmas</s>. [Cloth]
With necklaces, half-necklaces, bracelets of many kinds,
equipped with armlets and earrings —
mortals adorn themselves, having given to the disciples of the <s>Sugata</s>
variegated ornaments. [Ornaments]
Neither fire, nor poison enters the body of such a one,

children.text: na cāpi śastraṃ na tu vajravarṣam /
children.translated_text: nor weapons, nor a shower of thunderbolts —
through the gift of copper and other [vessels] in the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the <s>Jina</s>,
a mortal becomes one who dwells in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). [Copper and Other Vessels]

children.text: pūjyo vandyo bhavati manujo yatra yatropapannaḥ
children.translated_text: Worshipped and saluted is the person, wherever he is reborn;
having attained heaven, of great wealth, esteemed in righteous assemblies;
born in a brightly illustrious, very great family, of an enjoyment-loving nature —
he who gives a seat attains peace, possessed of incomparable virtues. [Seats]
Powerful, endowed with stability, a king of great prosperity —

children.text: saṃghasya bhojanaṃ dattvā sarvatra sukham edhate // bhojana
children.translated_text: having given food to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, one thrives in happiness everywhere. [Food]
One is born in a lofty family, virtuous,
attended by people, worthy of being seen,
pleasing, wise, happy, golden-hued,
prosperous — from the gift of rice and food-offerings. [Food Offerings]
Sweetmeats, <s>laḍḍukas</s> (laddoos), cakes, <s>paulikas</s> (pastries),
various <s>pūpas</s> (breads), <s>karambhakas</s> (porridges), and <s>parpaṭas</s> (thin wafers) —
one becomes devoted to enjoyments, a lord,
having given these mixed foods to the excellent assembly. [Sweets and Cakes]
Those people who, in vessels made of gold, silver, and the like,
place the finest yogurt, ghee, honey, sugar, and molasses
for the assembly and give them —
they become eaters of ambrosia, possessed of the five kinds of strength. [Five Essences]
Having filled a water-pot with water and given it to the excellent assembly,

children.text: pañca kāmaguṇān bhuktvā tṛṣṇāṃ chindanti śāśvatīm // kumbha
children.translated_text: having enjoyed the five strands of sensual pleasure, one cuts off thirst forever. [Water-Pot]
Through the gift of a water-vessel and bowl, one becomes endowed with knowledge of the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: dhanadena samāno 'sau jāyate ca triratnake // kuṇḍikāpātra
children.translated_text: equal to <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera, the god of wealth), one is born among the Three Jewels. [Water-Vessel and Bowl]

children.text: sarvaṃdadaś ca bhavati gṛhaṃ dattvā gaṇottame /
children.translated_text: One becomes a giver of all things, having given a house to the excellent assembly;

children.text: sarvakāmasamṛddhas tu sarvatra sukham edhate // gṛha
children.translated_text: rich in all desires, one thrives in happiness everywhere. [House]
Through the gift of a wish-fulfilling tree, one becomes complete by that very act;
one will be a human of <s>Uttarakuru</s>, of great enjoyments. [Wish-Fulfilling Tree]
Great are the benefits of the gift of a bell:
one becomes beautiful, of an ever-joyful mind,
with a voice pleasing to gods and <s>asuras</s> —
one is born equal to the king of the <s>Gandharvas</s>. [Bell]

children.text: yaḥ saṃghe pradadāti bhaiṣajavidhīṃs tāṃs tān prasannāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: One who gives various medical treatments to the <s>Saṃgha</s> with a serene intention —
he is not touched by sufferings arising from diseases and other calamities of existence;

children.text: mukto vyādhijarādibhiś ca sukhito jīvaty abhinnāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: freed from disease, old age, and the like, he lives happily with an undivided mind;
free from the illness of afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), he attains ultimate health.
In the past, one who had gone with medicine was turned away with [only] bark-cloth;

children.text: tatra saṃghe nirābādhe ca bhaiṣajyam ayācata //
children.translated_text: there, in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, free from affliction, he requested medicine.
By a single passion-free one, out of compassion for his benefit,

children.text: ekāṃ harītakīṃ bhuktvā tat karma samudāgamat // 2
children.translated_text: having eaten a single <s>harītakī</s> (myrobalan fruit), that <s>karma</s> came to fruition. (2)

body.text:
pañca janmaśatāny asya na rogaḥ svalpako 'py abhūt /
  kleśavyādhiṃ vivarjitya nirvṛttiś carame bhave // 3 // bhaiṣajya
body.translated_text: For five hundred births, not even the slightest illness befell him; having abandoned the illness of afflictions, [he attained] final release in his last existence. (3) [Medicine]

children.translated_text: Clear, without disagreeable smell, very light, endowed with sweetness, cool —

children.text: yo niryātayatīha vītarajase saṃghāya hṛdyaṃ jalam /
children.translated_text: one who here gives such pleasant water to the passion-free <s>Saṃgha</s>,
with pure body, speech, and mind, free from burning heat like a sword, happy —

children.text: tṛṣṇāṃ hanti na kevalaṃ vijahate saṃsāratṛṣṇāṃ api //
children.translated_text: he destroys not only [physical] thirst but abandons the thirst of <s>saṃsāra</s> as well.
In the dispensation of <s>Kāśyapa</s> [Buddha], by the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Yaśomitra</s>,
for twelve thousand years, water was distributed to the assembly.

body.text:
tena karmavipākena pañca janmaśatāny asau /
  na pipāsākṛtaṃ duḥkaṃ svapneṣv api anubhūtavān // 2 // jala
body.translated_text: Through the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, for five hundred births, he did not experience the suffering caused by thirst, even in dreams. (2) [Water]

children.text: ye saṃghe pratipādayanti muditās tṛṣṇācchidaṃ pānakaṃ
children.translated_text: Those who, with delight, offer to the <s>Saṃgha</s> a beverage that cuts off thirst,
pleasant, endowed with sweet flavor, of sharp taste, delightful in fragrance, and dear —
they, having cut with wisdom the creeper of craving, which produces the existence of passion for existence,

children.text: pāraṃ yānti bhavārṇavasya niyataṃ dattvā śubhaṃ pānakam // pānaka
children.translated_text: certainly cross to the far shore of the ocean of existence, having given the auspicious beverage. [Beverage]
Of those possessing unlimited wealth, equipped with horses and elephants,
with very many attendants — the palaces of kings —
having obtained the domain of the earth surrounded by oceans, a king of men
of supremely lovely beauty is born through the gift of land. [Land]
Variegated grains and other fruits and such —
one who, endowed with faith, gives them to the <s>Saṃgha</s>:
the desired fruits always ripen for him,
and all fruits ripen on the path to awakening. [Grain]
Merit is a lamp for people in darkness,
a protection in dangers, a kinsman in calamities,
an unsurpassed medicine in diseases,
and a raft in the great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Through giving come enjoyments, not through harming others;
through moral conduct comes heaven, not through jumping off cliffs;
through truthfulness comes purity, not through entering water;
through knowledge comes liberation, not through emaciation of the body.
Through not giving, one attains poverty;
from poverty, one commits sin;
having committed sin, one goes to hell;
released from hell, one is again a sinner.
Giving destroys poverty; moral conduct destroys lower births;
wisdom destroys ignorance; meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) destroys [rebirth in] existence.

children.text: śuddhena manasā dravyaṃ svaṃ dadāti yadā pumān /
children.translated_text: When a person gives his own possessions with a pure mind,
that very moment, the aggregate of wholesome [merit] — that is called giving.

children.text: lakṣmīr jājvalyamānā vasatu iha sadā kīrtir apy utsphurantī
children.translated_text: May blazing <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) dwell here always, and may radiant fame [be present];

children.text: niḥśeṣāriḥ kṣitīśaḥ kṣitim avatu ciraṃ vyādhidurbhikṣamuktām /
children.translated_text: may the king of the earth, with all enemies destroyed, long protect the land, freed from disease and famine;

children.text: śīlāḍhyā dakṣiṇīyāḥ pravacananicaye vṛddhim āyāntu nityam
children.translated_text: may those rich in moral conduct, worthy of offerings, always increase in the collection of the teaching;
may the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s> triumph, unshakable, as long as the moon and sun shine!
May the lord of the earth rule the earth with <s>Dharma</s>;
may the people become worshippers of the Three Jewels;
may families, with evil allayed and with abundant cattle, [be prosperous];
and may the people, blessed with good offspring, always rejoice!

children.text: vibhāti karabhāḥ suro nabhasi yāvad uṣṇaprabhaḥ
children.translated_text: As long as the sun, the warm-rayed one, the ray-maker, shines in the sky,
and the moon rises, tangled with radiance, marked with a hare;
as long as the lotus-dwelling ones [bloom] on the earth, unimpeded —
may the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>, worshipped by gods and <s>asuras</s>, endure!

body.text:
32 B
atha sthavirasthavirā bhikṣavaḥ / bhagavantaṃ paripṛcchanti / kiṃ bhagavatā karma kṛtaṃ / yasya karmaṇo vipākena bhagavato 'bhisaṃbuddhasya pāṣāṇāśarkarayā pādāṅguṣṭaḥ kṣataḥ / bhagavān āha / tathāgatenaiva bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānīti vistaraḥ / na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api sāmagrīm prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehināṃ / bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asaṃkhyeye 'nyatamasmin karvaṭakaviṣaye gṛhapatiḥ prativasati sma / tena sadṛśaṃ kalatram ānītaṃ / sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati / tasya krīḍato ramataḥ paricārayataḥ patny āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā / kālāntareṇāṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt putro jātaḥ / unnīto vardhito mahān saṃvṛttaḥ / athāpareṇa samayena tasya gṛhapateḥ patnī kālagatā / tenānyā patny ānītā tasya tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍato body.translated_text: Then the elder monks, the senior <s>bhikṣus</s>, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What <s>karma</s> did the <s>Bhagavān</s> perform, by the ripening of which <s>karma</s>, even after the <s>Bhagavān's</s> complete awakening, his big toe was injured by a stone splinter?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Bhikṣus</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself performed those deeds' — in detail: 'Actions do not perish even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>; when the right combination and time are met, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.' Once upon a time, <s>bhikṣus</s>, in the past, in a certain innumerable [age], in a certain market-town district, there lived a householder. He had taken a suitable wife. He sported, played, and amused himself with her. While he sported, played, and amused himself, his wife became pregnant. In due time, after eight or nine months, a son was born. He was nourished, raised, and grew up. Then, at another time, that householder's wife passed away. He took another wife. While he sported, played, and amused himself with her, a son was born. By him, the elder son was given a dwelling. While that one sported, played, and amused himself, a son was born and a daughter as well. Then, at another time, the householder, together with his wife, passed away. The [younger] boy remained in the care of that very elder brother. The householder's son was told by his wife: 'Noble husband, this boy [is here] — he is my brother[-in-law].' She said: 'Noble husband, his share of the household property must also be given.' He said: 'Half is his, half is ours.' She said: 'Noble husband, is it fitting that being one man he gets half, while we who are many get half?' He said: 'This is the way of the world.' She said: 'Noble husband, if it is so, have him killed.' He said: 'Good woman, how could I have my brother killed for the sake of property?' But she urged him again and again: 'For one who indulges in desires, there is nothing that should not be done as evil.' So he agreed. He said to his brother: 'Brother, let us go to the forest for the purpose of gathering flowers.' He went with him. There, in a mountain cave, having thrown him in, he killed him with a stone. What do you think, <s>bhikṣus</s>? That householder's son who had his half-brother killed for the sake of property — that was I myself at that time, on that occasion. Because I had my half-brother killed for the sake of property, through the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, for many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of years I was reborn in hells. Through the residue of that very <s>karma</s>, even now, the <s>Tathāgata's</s> foot, after complete awakening, was injured by a stone splinter.'

body.translated_text: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did the <s>Bhagavān</s> perform, by the ripening of which <s>karma</s>, the <s>Bhagavān's</s> foot, after complete awakening, was injured by a <s>khadira</s>-wood splinter?' '<s>Bhikṣus</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself performed those deeds' — in detail: Once upon a time, <s>bhikṣus</s>, two caravan leaders, having skillfully prepared an ocean-going vessel, descended into the great ocean as seekers of wealth. With a favorable wind they reached the Jewel Island. There, one of them filled his vessel to capacity, and the second only partially. They set out. Then the one whose vessel was only partially filled — his [goods] were ruined. That caravan leader, having weighed and removed the jewels with a scale, addressed the [other] caravan leader. He reflected: 'This one, whose purpose is fulfilled, will go away, while I, whose purpose has failed...' He began to bore a hole in the [other's] vessel. While he was boring, he was seen by the caravan leader, who said: 'Do not bore a hole in the vessel! Lest we all be plunged into calamity and disaster!' Though warned, he would not stop. So he was killed by the other with a spear-blow. What do you think, <s>bhikṣus</s>? That caravan leader who was killed by a spear-blow — that was I myself at that time, on that occasion. Because I killed him with a spear-blow, through the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, for many hundreds of years, for many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of years, I was reborn in hells. Through the residue of that very <s>karma</s>, the <s>Tathāgata's</s> diamond-like foot, after complete awakening, was injured by a <s>khadira</s>-wood splinter.'

body.translated_text: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did the <s>Bhagavān</s> perform, by the ripening of which <s>karma</s> the <s>Bhagavān</s>, after complete awakening, was falsely accused by the young woman <s>Sundarikā</s>?' '<s>Bhikṣus</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself performed and accumulated those deeds' — in detail — 'they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.' Once upon a time, <s>bhikṣus</s>, in the past, when the lifespan of beings was eighty thousand years, a Teacher named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened <s>Bhagavān</s>. Under the dispensation of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, two brothers had gone forth [as monks]: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Bharadvāja</s>. <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> had realized <s>Arhat</s>-ship through the abandonment of all afflictions. <s>Bharadvāja</s> too, by studying and reciting, had learned the three <s>Piṭakas</s> (scripture baskets). He became a master of the three <s>Piṭakas</s>, possessed of ready and apt eloquence. By him, a householder was converted. That [householder], on his account, had a monastery built, equipped with all requisites. That [<s>Bharadvāja</s>], learning that his brother had arrived, [said]: 'Come, let us arrange lodging together.' He [<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>] went there. He was seen by that householder. The <s>Arhat bhikṣu</s> was pleasing in body and pleasing in mind; seeing him, [the householder] was filled with faith. Having worshipped him, filled with devotion, he covered him with a valuable cloth. That [brother, <s>Bharadvāja</s>] saw this and [thought]: 'I am the one who takes precedence with this householder in everything. He covers him with cloth while I was [already] covered' — thus he became one looking for an opportunity [to defame] his [brother]. He [<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>] saw [<s>Bharadvāja</s>] was disturbed and reflected: 'If I give it to him, he will develop even greater faith' — and so he relinquished it to him, [saying]: 'Let it be yours.' That householder's servant girl used to come to that monastery to do service. He said to her: 'Girl, I give you this pair of garments. You must do what I say.' She said: 'Venerable one, what must I do?' 'You — having put on that pair of garments — do the household work. If the householder asks: "Where did you get this pair of garments?" you should say: "The venerable so-and-so gave it to me." If he asks: "For what purpose did the venerable one give it to you?" you should say: "This too the venerable one should be asked — for what purpose do men give things to women?"' She, having put on that cloth, began to do the household work. The householder recognized the cloth. He said to her: 'Girl, where did you get this pair of garments?' She said: 'The venerable so-and-so gave this to me.' 'Girl, for what reason did the venerable one give you this pair of garments?' She said: 'Venerable one, this too should be asked — for what reason do men give things to women?' He began to feel displeasure toward that [<s>Arhat</s>]. Those great beings are afraid of disrespect. He [the <s>Arhat</s>] got up and departed. What do you think, <s>bhikṣus</s>? That one named <s>Bharadvāja</s> who made the false accusation against that <s>Arhat</s> — that was I myself at that time, on that occasion. Because I falsely accused that <s>Arhat bhikṣu</s>, through the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, for many hundreds of thousands of years, for many hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of years, I was reborn in hells. Through the residue of that very <s>karma</s>, even now the <s>Tathāgata</s> was falsely accused by the young woman <s>Sundarikā</s>' — and so forth in detail.
